knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor When Direction Reverses

question.:question/problem:
The three vectors share an origin, and each grid square has the same side length.

![](9dd1efd7ebfaad7a95c994440a49.png)

If $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}-3\mathbf{b}$, then $\lambda=$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First trace $-3\mathbf{b}$ from the common origin $O$ to a point $P$: reverse its direction and scale its length. The remaining path from $P$ to the endpoint $C$ must be the unknown multiple of $\mathbf{a}$.

![](90fbb58be07f7d83fde72fbfd980.png)

Following the grid direction of $\mathbf{a}$ takes $4$ steps, while the parallel path $PC$ has $4$ steps. Their length ratio is $\frac{4}{4}=1$. The remaining path points in the opposite direction to $\mathbf{a}$, so
$$
\overrightarrow{PC}=-\mathbf{a}.
$$
Adding the path vectors gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c}&=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC}\\
&=-3\mathbf{b}+(-\mathbf{a})\\
&=-\mathbf{a}-3\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Because $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are nonparallel, these coefficients are unique. Comparing with $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}-3\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=-1$. The minus sign records the reversed direction.
